question.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=⟨t,\,1,\,\sqrt{2t}⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
question.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2t})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\times a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨t,\,1,\,\sqrt{2t}⟩\times ⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}}⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ t & 1 & \sqrt{2t} \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}}\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}1 & \sqrt{2t} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}}\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}t & \sqrt{2t} \\ 1 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}}\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}t & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}},\frac{\sqrt{2t}}{2},-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}||v|| & =\sqrt{{(t)}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}+{(\sqrt{2t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}+2t+1}, \\  & =\sqrt{(t+1)^{2}} \\  & =t+1, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}})}^{2}+{(\frac{\sqrt{2t}}{2})}^{2}+{(-1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{2t}+\frac{t}{2}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{t}^{2}+2t+1}{2t}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{(t+1)^{2}}{2t}} \\  & =\frac{t+1}{\sqrt{2t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{t+1}{\sqrt{2t}})}{t+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}}.\end{aligned}
$$
